body: I wonder if those should also be moved someplace else, so we don't have all these forward declares for core enums included all the codebase, when what we need is mostly the macro itself.

The macro itself could be moved to where `MAKE_ENUM_TYPE_INFO` is, which is `type_info.h`.
I'm not sure if would even need a separate `variant_caster.h` in this case.

> The macro itself could be moved to where `MAKE_ENUM_TYPE_INFO` is, which is `type_info.h`. 

Applied.

> I'm not sure if would even need a separate `variant_caster.h` in this case.

In fact, this header is specifically designed for `gdvirtual.gen.h`. It requires `VariantCaster` and these enum casts. If gdvirtual remains unchanged, removing the remaining references to `binder_common.h` is not very meaningful, because `gdvirtual.gen.h` will propagate `binder_common.h` into most compilation units.


> I wonder if those should also be moved someplace else, so we don't have all these forward declares for core enums included all the codebase, when what we need is mostly the macro itself.

I don’t really have a good idea where these should be placed. These declarations need to come after `type_info.h`, and `gdvirtual.gen.h` uses them (unless we ask downstream code to include the necessary declarations themselves, but that would result in pretty ugly template error messages).

I suppose if `gdvirtual.gen.h` doesn't compile without the enum casts, it does make sense to separate them out. the common binders are still included by `class_db.h`, which we do require an include for from `Object` compile units, so i guess there's no risk of granularization otherwise.
